The hostel common room went quiet as Devika's phone lit up with the video of her presentation and the caption that mocked her voice. Raghav, from her class, had shared it. Two hundred people had laughed.

Her face burned. She typed fast: a line about Raghav's marks and his boasting, sharp enough to cut. She posted it before anyone could stop her.

By dinner the reply had more views than the original. Someone had captured a screenshot and put it in the class group with a laughing face. The warden called Devika to the office the next morning, and the crowd now had fresh things to say about her, not only about the talk.

qa.a: Devika was humiliated and furious, with her face burning, and wanted to hurt back at once.

qa.a: Devika could delete the reply, avoid adding more, and ask a trusted adult to help handle the mockery, because stopping the fuel is what lets the attention fade.

Dear Sangeeta,
You asked why I went quiet online for a month. Here's the honest version.
After my cooking video got laughed at, one account kept posting the worst jokes. Each one stung more. On the fourth night I snapped and wrote a reply mocking his profile photo and calling him a "jobless loser who lives for this." It felt brilliant for about ten minutes.
Then his followers found it. By morning my reply had been reposted more times than the original video, with my face circled next to his. People who hadn't even seen the video were now arguing about me. Someone made a sticker out of my insult.
I gave them exactly what they wanted: a new, bigger story. I deleted the reply, but screenshots don't delete.
Next time I'll close the app instead. Tell me if I ever start to type like that again.
Madhuri

qa.a: It mocked the critic's profile photo and called him a 'jobless loser who lives for this'.

qa.q: How did Madhuri feel before and after posting the reply?
qa.a: Madhuri felt stung and angry before, briefly triumphant for ten minutes after, and then regretful once the reply spread.

qa.q: What would you change first in how Madhuri handled the mockery?
qa.a: I would close the app on the night it stung most and let a friend like Sangeeta read the reply before posting, because the insult became the bigger story.

qa.q: How might Sangeeta feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Sangeeta may feel sad for Madhuri but also trusted, since Madhuri asks to be stopped next time.

grounding: Shows the person hitting back at the main critic with an insult, which drew more attention and gave the crowd fresh material.

"Binita, you asked me to talk about the worst thing I did online, so here goes, from me, Gautam, the idiot of last March.
I'd posted a review of our college band's concert. It wasn't kind. A guy from the band quoted it and wrote, 'This from someone who can't hold a tune?' People piled on with clips of me singing at a birthday.
I was so embarrassed that I wanted to win. So I wrote the sharpest thing I could think of about his stammer on stage. I thought everyone would laugh with me.
Nobody did. Within an hour that post was all anyone talked about. The band's fans, people from other colleges, even my own friends were quoting it. The original review was forgotten; now the story was that I'd mocked someone's speech.
I apologised to him in person a week later. He accepted, barely. The screenshots are still out there."

qa.q: What did the band member's quote say about Gautam?
qa.a: It said, 'This from someone who can't hold a tune?'

qa.q: Why did Gautam write the cutting reply, and what was he feeling?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed by the clips and wanted to win, so pride pushed him to hit back as sharply as possible.

qa.q: What could Gautam have done instead when the clips appeared?
qa.a: He could have stayed off the thread for a day and, if needed, answered only the fair point about his review, which would have given the crowd nothing new.

qa.q: How might the band member have felt when Gautam mocked his stammer?
qa.a: He likely felt hurt and humiliated in front of many people, which may be why he only barely accepted the apology.

grounding: Shows the person answering mockery with a cutting remark about the critic, which drew more attention and turned the crowd's focus onto the insult.
